learn.hook: A rainbow is like a surprise gift after the rain. Poets love to write about it. Let's read a little rainbow poem!
points: A poem is written in lines. A group of lines is called a stanza.
Rhyming words end with the same sound: new-hue, bright-light, rain-train.
Poets use word pictures (imagery) so we can see, hear and feel what they describe.
Reading a poem aloud helps us enjoy its rhythm, like the beat of a song.
A poet may call one thing by another name, like calling a rainbow 'a painted bridge'.

example.q: Read the poem: After the rain, the sky is new, / A shining bow of every hue. / Red and orange, yellow bright, / Green and blue in golden light, / Indigo and violet too, / A painted bridge for me and you! Which words rhyme with 'too'?
steps: Look at the line that ends with 'too': 'Indigo and violet too'.
Look at the next line's last word: 'you'.
'Too' and 'you' end with the same sound.
example.answer: 'You' rhymes with 'too' (and 'new' and 'hue' have the same sound too).

learn.reallife: Songs, nursery rhymes and film songs all use rhyming words. That is why they are so easy to remember!

games.title: About the poem
items: In the poem, the rainbow comes after the rain.
The first line says, 'After the rain, the sky is new'.
The poem calls the rainbow 'a painted bridge'.
The last line calls it 'A painted bridge for me and you!'
The poem says the rainbow comes out at night.
The poem talks about golden light after the rain, not night.

quiz.q: Read: 'Red and orange, yellow bright, / Green and blue in golden light.' Which word rhymes with 'bright'?
quiz.explain: 'Bright' and 'light' both end with the same '-ight' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that is in the poem but does not sound the same at the end

quiz.q: Read: 'After the rain, the sky is new.' When does the rainbow appear in the poem?
quiz.explain: The first line says 'After the rain'.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the first line carefully

quiz.q: Read: 'A shining bow of every hue.' Why does the poet call the rainbow a 'bow'?
options: Because it is curved like a bow
Because it is straight like a stick
quiz.explain: An archer's bow is curved. The rainbow has the same curved shape.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture the shape the poet is comparing

quiz.q: Read: 'A shining bow of every hue.' What does 'hue' mean?
quiz.explain: Hue is another word for colour. 'Every hue' means every colour.
quiz.mistake: Guesses the meaning without using clues from the poem

quiz.q: Read: 'Red and orange, yellow bright, / Green and blue in golden light, / Indigo and violet too.' How many rainbow colours are named?
quiz.explain: It names red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet: 7 colours. 'Golden' describes the light, not a rainbow colour.
quiz.mistake: Misses a colour or counts 'golden' as a rainbow colour

quiz.q: Which pair of words rhymes?
quiz.explain: 'Rain' and 'train' end with the same '-ain' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks words that go together in meaning instead of in sound

quiz.q: What is a group of lines in a poem called?
quiz.explain: Poems are made of stanzas. Stories are made of paragraphs.
quiz.mistake: Uses the word for stories instead of poems

quiz.q: Read: 'A shining bow of every hue.' Which word tells us the rainbow is bright?
quiz.explain: 'Shining' describes how bright the rainbow looks.
quiz.mistake: Picks the naming word instead of the describing word

teach.ask: Gappu looks at the sky: 'What are rhyming words? And what is a word picture in a poem?'
teach.praise: What a colourful explanation! My feathers are glowing like a rainbow!
teach.nudge: How do I know two words rhyme? And what does a word picture do?

learn.hook: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red. Say VIBGYOR fast three times!
points: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through raindrops in the air.
Sunlight is made of seven colours. We remember their order as VIBGYOR.
To see a rainbow, stand with the sun behind you and the rain in front of you.
A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as': as green as a parrot; the rainbow is like a bridge.
Word pictures (imagery) help the reader see, hear, smell, taste or feel something.

example.q: Complete the simile: 'The mango leaves are as green as a ___.' Choose from: parrot, crow, cloud.
steps: A simile compares two things that share something.
We need something that is green.
A parrot is green; a crow is black and a rain cloud is grey.

learn.reallife: After a monsoon shower in the evening, look at the sky away from the sun. You may spot a rainbow!

quiz.q: In VIBGYOR, what colour does the letter V stand for?
quiz.explain: VIBGYOR starts with violet. Note the spelling: v-i-o-l-e-t.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up violet with similar-sounding words

quiz.q: In VIBGYOR, which colour comes between green and orange?
quiz.explain: V-I-B-G-Y-O-R: after G (green) comes Y (yellow), then O (orange).
quiz.mistake: Forgets the order of the letters

quiz.q: When can we see a rainbow?
options: When there are no clouds or water
quiz.explain: A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through tiny drops of water in the air.
quiz.mistake: Does not know a rainbow needs both sunlight and water drops

quiz.q: Where should the sun be when you look at a rainbow?
quiz.explain: We see a rainbow when the sun is behind us and the raindrops are in front of us.
quiz.mistake: Thinks you must look towards the sun to see a rainbow

quiz.q: Which sentence is a simile?
options: Her smile was as bright as the sun.
quiz.explain: It compares her smile with the sun using 'as ... as'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any sentence with a describing word is a simile

quiz.q: Complete the simile: 'as black as ___'
quiz.explain: Coal is black, so 'as black as coal' makes sense. Milk, snow and cotton are white.
quiz.mistake: Picks a thing that does not share the quality

quiz.q: On the outside edge of a rainbow, which colour do we usually see?
quiz.explain: In a rainbow, red is on the outer edge and violet is on the inner edge.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bow starts with V because VIBGYOR does

quiz.q: Which sentence paints the best word picture?
options: Peacocks danced in the silver rain.
quiz.explain: 'Peacocks danced in the silver rain' helps us see colours and movement. That is imagery.
quiz.mistake: Picks a short, plain sentence that gives no picture

teach.ask: Gappu sings: 'What is VIBGYOR? And what is a simile?'
teach.praise: Seven colours and a simile! I feel as happy as a bird in the rain!
teach.nudge: Which colours are in VIBGYOR? And what words does a simile use?

learn.hook: The sky is bright. The rainbow is brighter. The sun is the brightest! Let's learn how describing words change.
points: Describing words (adjectives) tell us more about a noun: a colourful rainbow, five birds, a happy child.
To compare two things, we add -er or use 'more': brighter, more beautiful.
To compare more than two things, we add -est or use 'most': brightest, most beautiful.
Some words change completely: good-better-best, bad-worse-worst.

example.q: Choose: 'The rainbow is ___ than the grey clouds.' (bright, brighter, brightest)
steps: We are comparing two things: the rainbow and the clouds.
For two things we use the -er form.
The word 'than' also tells us to use the -er form.

learn.reallife: In shops we hear, 'This one is cheaper,' and in sports, 'She is the fastest runner.' That is comparing!

quiz.q: Which word is an adjective in: 'A colourful rainbow appeared.'?
quiz.explain: 'Colourful' describes the rainbow, so it is an adjective.
quiz.mistake: Picks the noun or the verb

quiz.q: What is the comparative form of 'big'?
quiz.explain: Double the 'g' and add -er: bigger. 'Biggest' is the superlative.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the last letter

quiz.q: What is the superlative form of 'good'?
quiz.explain: Good changes completely: good, better, best.
quiz.mistake: Adds -est to an irregular adjective

quiz.q: Choose: 'Today is the ___ day of the year.' (hot)
quiz.explain: We compare one day with all the days of the year, so we use the superlative: hottest.
quiz.mistake: Uses the -er form when comparing more than two

quiz.q: Choose: 'The sky looks ___ than yesterday.' (clear)
quiz.explain: Two things are compared and the word 'than' is used, so we need 'clearer'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'more' and '-er' together

quiz.q: What is the superlative form of 'beautiful'?
quiz.explain: Long words use 'most' for the superlative: most beautiful.
quiz.mistake: Adds -est to a long word

quiz.q: What is the comparative form of 'pretty'?
quiz.explain: Change y to i and add -er: prettier.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the 'y' when adding -er

quiz.q: Which comparing sentence is correct?
options: An elephant is heavyer than a goat.
An elephant is more heavier than a goat.
An elephant is heavier than a goat.
An elephant is heaviest than a goat.
quiz.explain: 'Heavier' is the right comparative, and it goes with 'than'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up spelling rules or uses two comparatives together

teach.ask: Gappu puffs up: 'I am big, my mother is bigger. How do describing words change when we compare?'
teach.praise: Best explanation ever! That is the superlative, you know!
teach.nudge: Which ending do we use for two things? And which for more than two?
